fair_value_reasoning: Unsized screen. The rule names no NVIDIA sales figure. Ceiling: the 'Other' region was 2.2% of FY26 Data Center revenue (per tonight's sector readthrough); these seven entities are a part of it, and the 10-K region tables do not break them out. Assuming they took no more than about a quarter of that ceiling (~0.5% of Data Center, booked in acie) and value moves roughly one-for-one with Data Center revenue gives about -0.5% to the research target (12m). The larger, unsized risk is a wider SE Asia rule or tighter licensing that follows this one; the Dec 1/3 congressional hearings are the next dated step.
breaks: The 11-10 decided acie card's premise that no rule is in force against SE Asian intermediaries; ACIE (AI cloud / sovereign) revenue path
trigger_hit: Board investigation finds a security compromise, or Commerce suspends licences to SE Asian intermediaries (Chip Security Act or the Banks/Warren request) -- check: BIS rule or licence action naming Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam or Singapore (BIS Entity List rule 2026-23999, 11-23)
summary: The Commerce Department (BIS) added seven Malaysian, Singapore and Thai firms, including the Megaspeed group and Alibaba-owned Apex, to the Entity List on Nov 23 with a presumption of denial for all US items, citing diversion risk for advanced chips. That is the research's Southeast Asia licence trigger; it is already flagged for NVIDIA's next update, and the revenue at stake looks small (the whole 'Other' region was 2.2% of FY26 Data Center). Today's ~7% drop is a giveback of Monday's 31% rebound on Jensen Huang's return, with no new NVIDIA filing.

items.headline: BIS adds 7 entities to the Entity List (Malaysia: MSFusion, PT Megaspeed International, Speedmatrix; Singapore: Apex Enterprise Solutions (Alibaba-owned), Megaspeed International, Swiftdata; Thailand: Megaspeed (Thailand)); licence required for all EAR items, presumption of denial, 30-day savings clause; FR publication 11-25
items.why: Opened the Federal Register public-inspection text: cites significant risk of diverting advanced computing commodities (names neither NVIDIA nor China). Matches the thesis trigger on a BIS action naming Malaysia, Thailand or Singapore; hits acie. Already flagged for NVDA's next round.
